reference_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_products
FROM products
WHERE sku <> UPPER(TRIM(sku))
alternatives: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sku <> UPPER(TRIM(sku))) AS n_products FROM products
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_products FROM products WHERE NOT (sku = TRIM(UPPER(sku)))
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN sku = UPPER(TRIM(sku)) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS n_products FROM products

other_way.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE sku <> UPPER(TRIM(sku))) AS n_products FROM products
other_way.tradeoff: A FILTER count keeps every product in the query, which helps when a second count joins it, but WHERE is shorter for one.
